title: ci: adopt fleet v1 workflows (agent review plus the Fable second review, merge gate, security scans, verify flows, screenshot diff, mining, sync)
body:
Key `RW-FLEET-WORKFLOWS`

**Context**
Runway carries its own copies of what fleet now provides: `.github/workflows/agent-review.yml`, `.github/scripts/agent_review.py`, `.github/scripts/agent-review-run.sh`, `.github/agent-review/`, `merge-gate.yml` + `.github/scripts/merge-gate.sh`, `security.yml`, `verify.yml` ("Verify flows"), `screenshot-diff.yml` + `tools/screenshot_diff.py`, `cancel-on-close.yml`, `tidy-releases.yml`. This issue replaces them with callers of fleet's reusable workflows, pinned by SHA. Runway releases on every push to `main`, so this lands as one PR titled `ci: …`.

The header of today's `agent-review.yml` records an owner decision: "every review uses Sonnet and never Opus, security-sensitive changes included". The first review stays Sonnet; the owner has since decided that risky pull requests also get a second review by Fable. That new decision is recorded in fleet's workflow header and in this PR's description.

This PR changes `.github/workflows/agent-review.yml`, but `pull_request_target` runs main's copy, so the new second review first runs on the next PR; the owner reviews this one by hand (CODEOWNERS covers `.github/`).

**Scope**
- `.github/workflows/agent-review.yml` → a caller: `pull_request_target` on `main` with `[opened, synchronize, reopened, ready_for_review, labeled, unlabeled]`; secrets `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` passed by name; budgets from `vars.AGENT_REVIEW_BUDGET_USD`/`AGENT_REVIEW_MAX_TURNS` as today; `generated`: `docs/openapi.json`, `frontend/src/lib/api-types.ts`, `docs/feature-map.json`, `docs/src/content/docs/contributing/feature-map.md`, `tests/fixtures/forecast_golden.json` (listed explicitly, so it stays out of the diff even though it sits under `tests/fixtures/`); `second-review-paths` below.
- Second-review paths (`.github/**` and `.claude/**` are built in): `runway/oidc.py`, `runway/applock.py`, `runway/tls.py`, `runway/money.py`, `runway/storage/secretbox.py`, `runway/storage/backup.py`, `runway/domain/forecast.py`, `runway/providers/plaid*.py`, `runway/providers/simplefin.py`, `runway/providers/sfinvest.py`, `runway/providers/carta*.py`, `runway/server/handler.py`, `runway/server/routes.py`, `runway/server/sync.py`, `runway/server/mcp_*.py`, `runway/server/oauth_http.py`, `runway/server/api/connections.py`, `runway/server/api/lock.py`, `runway/server/api/backups.py`, `extension/**`, `frontend/src/lib/api.ts`, `.semgrep/**`, `SECURITY.md`.
- `.github/agent-review/context.md` (new, from today's `prompt.md` wording): Runway is a personal finance app; private data is balances, amounts, merchants and payees, account and card names, lenders, budgets, income, dates of real transactions and people's names; tests use made-up figures; demo data is `runway/domain/demo.py`.
- `.github/agent-review/invariants.md` (new): Runway has no promises section, so list what the second review must hold, each with its check or "none yet": bank and provider credentials only decrypted in the storage layer (`secretbox`, Semgrep); every new session, grant, token or key ends when its owner can't sign in (`oidc.access_lapsed`); the half cent only as `money.CENT` (Semgrep); the forecast's results change only with `tests/fixtures/forecast_golden.json` and a reason; the app lock guards every route it says it guards; nothing private in logs (`monitoring.scrub`); HTTP only through `tls.urlopen` (Semgrep). Items marked "none yet" are candidates for `review-mining`.
- Delete `.github/scripts/agent_review.py`, `.github/scripts/agent-review-run.sh`, `.github/agent-review/{prompt.md,schema.json,incremental.md,package.json,package-lock.json}`, `.github/scripts/merge-gate.sh`, `tools/screenshot_diff.py`, `tests/test_agent_review.py` (moved to fleet), and the `/.github/agent-review` npm entry in `.github/dependabot.yml`.
- `merge-gate.yml` → a caller: keeps `workflow_run` of `Docker image`, `Security scans`, `Docs`, `Verify flows`, `check_suite` and `workflow_dispatch`; `ignored-workflows` `Preview|Screenshot diff`; `required-workflows` `Docker image`, `Security scans`, `CodeQL`; `required-statuses` `Agent review`, `Second review`.
- `security.yml` → a caller: `code-paths` `^(runway|frontend/src|extension|\.semgrep)/`, web dependencies `^frontend/package(-lock)?\.json$` (`web-dirs` `frontend`), `image-paths` `^(Dockerfile|\.dockerignore|pyproject\.toml|poetry\.lock)$`, the weekly cron kept in the caller.
- `verify.yml` → a caller of fleet's `verify.yml` running what it runs today (`run.py verify` and `frontend/verify/control-smoke.mjs`, through `make` targets added here if missing), same `paths:`, job still "Verify flows". `screenshot-diff.yml` → a caller (`dir: screenshots/`). `cancel-on-close.yml` (with the verify group) and `tidy-releases.yml` → callers. `preview.yml` stays Runway's own.
- New callers: `review-mining.yml` (monthly), `deep-scan-due.yml` (quarterly, `cron: "17 7 3 1,4,7,10 *"`), `fleet-sync.yml` (push to `main` on `.github/workflows/**`, weekly, by hand; `FLEET_BOT_APP_ID` variable and `FLEET_BOT_PRIVATE_KEY` secret by name).
- `.github/dependabot.yml`: the github-actions entry gains the `fleet` group.
- `docs/src/content/docs/contributing/development.md`: the review section describes both statuses and the Fable second review, with fleet's docs link.
- Owner, before merging: create the labels `security`, `safety-critical`, `manual`, `fleet`, `review-mining` (none exist in Runway).

**Out of scope**
`AGENTS.md`, `tools/`, `.claude/`, `Makefile` and `docker.yml`'s fleet-checks job (`RW-FLEET-CONTENT`). `CLAUDE.md` stays as it is.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] No copy of fleet's scripts, prompts or `screenshot_diff.py` remains (`git grep` finds only docs pointing at fleet).
- [ ] Every fleet reference SHA-pinned with a `# v1.x.y` comment, all at one version; `make fleet-checks` (today's checks) and zizmor pass.
- [ ] After merge: a throwaway agent PR touching `runway/money.py` gets "Agent review", "Second review" and "Merge gate"; a UI throwaway PR gets the Screenshot diff comment and runs Verify flows. Links pasted here; the owner closes them.
- [ ] `review-mining` run by hand creates "Repeated review findings".

**Tests**
`make fleet-checks`, `zizmor .github/workflows`, the throwaway PRs.

**Depends on**
`AnthonyPluth/fleet` v1.0.0 (fleet issue `FLEET-RELEASE`); `FLEET-SETUP` done (App installed, secrets set).

**Model**
Fable (`claude-fable-5-1`): review workflows, CI secrets and untrusted pull request content.

title: chore: adopt fleet v1 content (shared tools, vendored skills and hook, AGENTS.md shared sections with the repeated-mistake rule)
body:
Key `RW-FLEET-CONTENT`

**Context**
After {{RW-FLEET-WORKFLOWS}}, Runway still carries `tools/fleet_checks.py`, `tools/test_timings.py`, `.github/scripts/next-version.sh` and `.claude/hooks/session-start.sh`, and its `AGENTS.md` repeats sections fleet now owns. Cloud sessions don't install plugins a repository declares, so fleet's skills, reviewer agent and hook arrive as vendored files (`tools/fleet sync`, checked by `tools/fleet drift`).

Two behaviour changes come with fleet's union, both stated in the PR description: Runway gains Waypoint's check that a removed or skipped test carries a `Removes-Test:` or `Skips-Test:` trailer; and fleet's "Git and PRs" block says to open a PR for every change once it's pushed (Runway's "Open a PR only when asked" goes: every push to `main` releases, so all work lands through PRs).

**Scope**
- `pyproject.toml` gains `[tool.fleet]` with Runway's values: migrations `runway/storage/migrations/versions`, migration tests `tests/test_migrations.py`, tested-from `0036`, image homes `extension/icons/`, `runway/static/`, image file `docs/src/assets/logo.png`, screenshots `screenshots/` named from pages and flows (`frontend/verify/verify.mjs`, `frontend/verify/flows`), skills `.claude/skills`, the generated `verify-runway` references, `extra-checks = "tools.app_checks:CHECKS"`. No `[tool.fleet.no-comments]` (Runway's convention is to match the surrounding comment density) and no coverage floor (none today; a separate decision).
- `tools/app_checks.py` (new): the a11y baseline checks (shrink-only against main, every line still occurring) and the flow-inheritance check, moved out of `tools/fleet_checks.py`, with `tests/test_app_checks.py`.
- Delete `tools/fleet_checks.py`, `tools/test_timings.py`, `.github/scripts/next-version.sh` and `tests/test_fleet_checks.py`.
- `Makefile`: `fleet-checks` → `tools/fleet checks --commits origin/main..HEAD` then `tools/fleet drift` (so `make pre-push` keeps working); `test-timings` → `tools/fleet test-timings`; a `fleet-sync` target.
- `.github/workflows/docker.yml`: its fleet-checks job becomes a caller of fleet's `checks.yml`; the release version from `tools/fleet next-version`.
- `tools/fleet sync --to v1.x.y`: `.fleet/version`, `tools/fleet`, `.claude/skills/fleet-*`, `.claude/agents/fleet-reviewer.md`, `.claude/hooks/fleet-session-start.sh`, AGENTS.md blocks. `.claude/hooks/fleet.conf`: `PYTHON_VERSION=3.14`, `FRONTEND_DIRS="frontend"`, `APT_PACKAGES="libfaketime"`, `NODE_CHECK` naming `esrap` and `eslint-plugin-svelte` (today's completeness check). `.claude/settings.json`: SessionStart → the vendored hook; `extraKnownMarketplaces.fleet` pinned; no `enabledPlugins`. Delete `.claude/hooks/session-start.sh`.
- `AGENTS.md`: fleet blocks for "Starting work", "Working in a container", "Mistakes that keep coming back", "Git and PRs". Outside them Runway keeps: the CI-only bullet and the forecast-test bullet in "Working in a container", its own mistakes after the block (Tests that share the database, Private data in logs, Personal financial data in the repo, Time zones), the screenshots bullet in "Git and PRs", "Before you push" whole, and the conventions bullet on tests gains "when one really goes, a `Removes-Test:` or `Skips-Test:` trailer says why (checked)". `.claude/skills/verify-runway/` stays.

**Out of scope**
`CLAUDE.md` (routing unchanged); the verify driver and `tools/control`.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] `make check` and `make pre-push` pass; `tools/fleet drift` is clean.
- [ ] Editing one character inside a fleet block or a vendored file fails `make fleet-checks` (shown, then reverted).
- [ ] A fresh cloud session runs the vendored hook, including the `node_modules` completeness check, then `make lint` and `make frontend-check` start cleanly (output pasted).
- [ ] The a11y baseline still only shrinks: a PR adding a baseline line fails (test in `tests/test_app_checks.py`).

**Tests**
`tests/test_app_checks.py`, `make check`, `make pre-push`.

**Depends on**
{{RW-FLEET-WORKFLOWS}}; `AnthonyPluth/fleet` v1.0.0 (fleet issue `FLEET-RELEASE`).

**Model**
Opus: moves tools and instructions; no secrets or review workflows.

title: feat: loopback fakes for SimpleFIN and price quotes, so make verify and tools/control can drive Connect and Sync now
body:
Key `RW-PROVIDER-FAKES`

**Context**
`make verify` and `tools/control` run the demo server on made-up data with every outbound request sent to a dead proxy (`runway/verify.py`: `NO_OUTSIDE`, `clean_env`, `NO_PROXY=127.0.0.1,localhost`). No provider is faked: connecting SimpleFIN, Sync now, a sync that fails (expired access, server error) and the price refresh can't be exercised in the app, only in unit tests that patch the provider (`runway/providers/simplefin.py`'s `sync(..., fetch=fetch_accounts)`). An agent changing sync or connection screens therefore trusts tests instead of running the app. SimpleFIN is plain HTTPS with a claim URL and an access URL; prices already read `RUNWAY_PRICES_URL` (`runway/providers/prices.py`). Plaid stays out: its Link widget loads from Plaid's CDN, and Plaid's sandbox is the owner's manual check.

**Scope**
- `tests/fakes/simplefin_server.py`: an HTTPS server on 127.0.0.1 with a throwaway CA and certificate made per run in the run's temporary directory; serves the SimpleFIN protocol: `POST /claim/<token>` returning an access URL with basic auth, `GET /accounts?start-date=&end-date=` with made-up accounts and transactions consistent with `demo.seed`; a mode switch (`ok`, `401`, `403`, `500`, `slow`, `partial`) through `POST /__fake/mode`; records requests for tests.
- `tests/fakes/prices_server.py`: the chart reply shape `prices.py` parses, for the made-up symbols the demo holds.
- `runway/verify.py`: when `RUNWAY_VERIFY_FAKES=1` (set by `run.py verify` and `tools/control start`), start both fakes beside each demo server; in that server's environment only, set `SSL_CERT_FILE` to the system bundle plus the throwaway CA, add the fake's host to `NO_PROXY`, set `RUNWAY_PRICES_URL`, and point the demo's SimpleFIN connection at the fake. `providers/simplefin.py`'s https-only rule is unchanged; everything else still goes to the dead proxy.
- Flows in `frontend/verify/flows/`: `simplefin-connect` (Settings → paste a made-up setup token → accounts appear), `sync-now` (Sync now → the new made-up transactions show), `sync-reconnect` (mode `401` → the reconnect message); screenshots at phone and desktop. They show existing screens only: a needed layout, flow or copy change is out of scope and needs the owner's sign-off first.
- `.claude/skills/verify-runway/references/journeys.md`: a "drive a bank sync against the fake" recipe; `feature-gotchas.md`: what the fakes cover and what they don't (Plaid, Carta, Realie, Finnhub's stream); `make user-feature-map`.

**Out of scope**
Plaid, Carta, Realie, Finnhub; any UI change.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] The three flows pass in `make verify` and `make verify-twice` (identical images); images committed through `make screenshots`.
- [ ] A test asserts the only `NO_PROXY` addition is the fakes' loopback host, and that the throwaway CA exists only under the run's temporary directory and never in the image or the repository.
- [ ] `tests/test_simplefin.py` gains an end-to-end case against the fake over real TLS (claim, sync, a 401).
- [ ] `tools/control start` then `flow sync-now` works in a cloud session (output pasted).

**Tests**
`tests/test_simplefin.py`, `tests/test_verify_fakes.py`, the flows.

**Depends on**
Nothing (independent of the fleet adoption).

**Model**
Fable (`claude-fable-5-1`): the bank-connection path and TLS trust for the demo server.

title: Owner runbook: deep security scans with claude-security (first run, then quarterly)
body:
Key `RW-DEEP-SCAN`

**Context**
A deep scan with the claude-security plugin can't run in a workflow: the plugin asks a cost confirmation that only the person's own request can answer, refuses in a non-interactive session, and needs a live session (fleet's `docs/deep-scan.md`). fleet's `deep-scan-due` workflow, scheduled quarterly by {{RW-FLEET-WORKFLOWS}}, opens the reminder issue. Runway is public and holds bank access, so findings never go into a public issue.

**Scope**
- Follow fleet's `docs/deep-scan.md`: a local session in a fresh clone of `main`, `/model claude-fable-5-1`, "scan the whole repository at high effort" with your own sentence accepting the time and token cost.
- When: once after {{RW-FLEET-WORKFLOWS}} lands, then each time a "Deep security scan due" issue opens, and before any new bank or brokerage provider ships.
- Findings: one draft security advisory per confirmed finding; fixes through the advisory's private fork, or a neutral-titled PR labelled `security` once you decide.
- Record here only the revision stamp's file name, the effort and counts by severity.

**Out of scope**
Fixing findings.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] First scan run; stamp, effort and counts recorded here.
- [ ] Every HIGH or CRITICAL finding has a draft advisory.
- [ ] The report directory was not committed.

**Tests**
None (runbook).

**Depends on**
{{RW-FLEET-WORKFLOWS}}.

**Model**
Owner (no coding model); the scan itself runs on Fable 5.1.
